description: Unauthorized Access to Knowledge Base S3 Bucket Attackers could exploit misconfigured bucket policies, overly permissive IAM roles, or leaked AWS credentials to access sensitive documents in the S3 bucket. An attacker obtains AWS credentials from a public code repository or through a compromised system and uses them to download sensitive documents from the S3 bucket.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement strict S3 bucket access controls
recommendation: Enable S3 bucket logging and monitoring

description: Token Exposure in Client-Side Storage Storing authentication tokens in browser localStorage or sessionStorage makes them vulnerable to XSS attacks and malicious browser extensions. An attacker exploits an XSS vulnerability to inject JavaScript that extracts authentication tokens from localStorage and sends them to a malicious server.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1528 - Steal Application Access Token
recommendation: Implement token security best practices

description: PII Exposure Through AI Responses The AI model might include PII in its responses or store sensitive information in chat history, leading to potential privacy violations. A user asks questions that prompt the AI to reveal PII from the knowledge base or previous conversations.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1213 - Data from Information Repositories
recommendation: Implement AI guardrails and PII detection
